framework.name: Strengthening Systems
framework.description:
Result 2.1: National capacities are strengthened and use data for efficient crisis response and recovery planning. Indicative intervention areas:
•	Data generation to inform recovery planning and implementation: In partnership with the government and relevant line ministries and authorities the UN will support sector assessments that will be used to inform national recovery planning and implementation. Examples include assessments related to human impact, war damage, gender, protection, monitoring environmental impact of war, energy systems, WASH systems, market and value chain, agri-business, forestry, nuclear installations, etc. 
•	Institutional capacity development for national partners: The government’s strong response to the impact of the war has demonstrated that past investments in institutions have resulted in strong systems. The UN will continue to support government institutions and ministries to further grow capacity and adapt and adjust to the new challenging context. Key sectors targeted for support and institutional capacity development include security, justice, agriculture, education, health, social protection, and environment sectors. The focus of capacity strengthening will be on leading crisis management, emergency response and recovery planning and implementation. Government capacity for protecting and monitoring human rights and documenting violations, and implementing commitments under the Women, Peace and Security Agenda and Youth, Peace and Security Agenda, will also be supported as will strengthening capacity of local civil society and volunteer groups to participate and engage in emergency response and early recovery. Provision of technical expertise for macro-economic forecasting and policy advocacy from an LNOB perspective will also be a focus area.

Result 2.2: Early recovery interventions are effective in increasing inclusive human development, promoting a sustainable green economy and building a resilient society. Indicative intervention areas:

•	Infrastructure Reconstruction: Mine action, debris removal, reconstruction of critical infrastructure (health centres, schools, WASH, agriculture, IT, etc), implementation of affordable housing solutions.
•	Social Protection: Support to strengthening national social protection systems, including child protection systems, and promotion of alignment of multipurpose cash assistance to existing national systems.  
•	Education: Safe, secure and inclusive learning, integrated approaches to psychosocial support, social and emotional learning, and life skills education, continuity of learning, reintegration of teachers, researchers and scientists.
•	Health: Recovery and transformation of health systems, including access to pharmaceuticals and vaccinations, cold chain systems strengthening, WASH systems, digital healthcare solutions to improve access to and the quality of maternal and child healthcare services, support to mental health services, and prosthetics for victims of war.  
•	Food Security:  Maintain critical food production systems and support agri-food supply chains, markets and exports. Expand capacity for agricultural product storage and export.
•	Livelihoods and Economic Growth: Income solutions for IDPs, war affected and most vulnerable, support to affected women and youth in livelihoods recovery, skills development, business support, entrepreneurship training, access to finance, networks, markets and culture. Mobilize the private sector in humanitarian response. Strengthen labour market governance focusing on decent work. Sustainable industrial recovery, development of competitive and resource-efficient processing industries.
•	Energy and Environment: Winterization, mitigating the energy crisis, preparedness for next heating season. Connecting buildings to energy monitoring tools and energy efficient technologies. Support to energy system repair and reconstruction. Environmental clean-up and remediation, clean transport and green reconstruction. Promote bio-energy use in agriculture, sustainable natural resource management. Sustainable and inclusive environmental governance and advocacy on environmental impact of war.

projects.description:
UNHCR and partners repair homes through various modalities, including prefabricated core homes for families whose houses were completely destroyed.  Support is provided either directly to the household following a technical assessment or in partnership with the local authorities who work alongside UNHCR partners to assess the damage and the corresponding need and help distribute the materials and provide technical support. This modality is cost efficient and allows the homeowner to manage the repairs.  It is also fast and allows UNHCR to respond in a timely manner. 

 

In addition, as UNHCR is unable to address all barriers to durable solutions for displacement itself, it prioritizes locations and interventions in key thematic areas based on key considerations and build on UNHCR’s comparative advantage to achieve durable solutions to displacement. While some of these barriers are addressed under other areas (access to housing, access to justice and documentation and community empowerment and participation, and livelihoods), UNHCR will also ensure support to the forcibly displaced to access to services/infrastructure: support to infrastructure rehabilitation and reconstruction of public service premises, such as education, health, social protection, energy, etc. and provide support and capacity building to government social protection services, with a focus on meeting the needs of displaced persons as well as the particularly vulnerable groups.

projects.name: Supporting the system of psychological care and support (MHPSS) in the national education system in Ukraine
projects.description:
Evidence shows that Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) is critical in emergency and recovery contexts after exposure to trauma. It can promote emotional regulation, relational skills, effective communication, collaboration, compassion, empathy, and conflict resolution in educational contexts.

UNESCO is working alongside the Ministry of Education and Science to transform the provision of MHPSS inside the school system as part of the nationwide plan to enhance MHPSS in light of current and future challenges, led by First Lady Olena Zelenska.

This initiative adopts a three-domain approach of reforming policy, strengthening capacity, and creating supportive MHPSS tools and materials. Under this initiative, UNESCO will work with local implementation partners to train 15,000 school psychologists, 20,000 school personnel, parents, and caretakers, and reach 160,000 vulnerable children.

projects.name: Emergency livelihood and energy assistance for vulnerable farmers and small/medium-scale agro-processing industries in newly accessible and other conflict-affected areas of Ukraine
projects.description:
Crop and livestock production is maintained, access to income increased and energy supply restored among targeted rural communities affected by the war.
, FAO will, in close collaboration with the government and key partners, procure, distribute, support the installation of, and build the capacity of relevant small to medium farmers on the maintenance of power generators. The main sectors that will be targeted under the project are animal husbandry, fisheries (including aquaculture), and other related agro-processing industries. This will ultimately support the daily operability of core food/agro-processing industries where energy supply is either limited or non-existent. As a result, this will enable rural communities to access local food sources and, in turn, will enable local small/medium-scale farmers to continue to generate income. 
The generators aim to support the continuity of energy supply in over seven conflict-affected regions, which serve up to 25 percent of the population (approx. 9 million people). projects.description:
UNESCO World Water Quality Portal in the Dnipro River, Ukraine: Water quality monitoring using Earth observation satellites and in-situ measurements to ensure clean water for populations and human settlements.
Considering the importance of clean water for populations in human settlements in conflict-affected areas, in humanitarian response and in the long-term perspective, UNESCO proposes the application of the UNESCO World Water Quality Portal for operational water quality monitoring in a Dnipro River Basin area via Earth observation satellites with the aim at helping Ukrainian people have insight into the quality of water of the Dnipro River and the reservoirs along the Dnipro River, which provide water supplies to major cities of Ukraine, including the capital city Kyiv. Hence, the project provides vital information on the quality and safety of the water for the local populations and internally displaced persons relying upon for drinking, cooking and personal hygiene during the conflict.
The operational application of the UNESCO World Water Quality Portal in Dnipro River in Ukraine will enable water quality monitoring via the use of Earth observation satellites and in-situ measurements and as a result will provide valuable data and information on water quality of the Dnipro River and the reservoirs along the river. Water quality data retrieved from Earth observation satellite images will be calibrated. The availability of (historic or new) in-situ water quality monitoring data in the project area is highly recommended to ensure the calibration and scientific validation of the algorithms and satellite-retrieved data.

projects.name: Monitoring of Cultural Heritage Sites, Museums and Historic Cities in Ukraine via Satellite Imagery
projects.description: This project aimed at monitoring, via satellite imagery, cultural heritage sites and museums in Ukraine for any damage, losses, or destructions which have – or may occur – as a result of the hostilities. In addition, priority cities in Ukraine – Chernihiv, Kharkiv, Mariupol, Odesa, Kherson and Kyiv – will also be monitored at the urban level. To do so, UNESCO and UNITAR through its Programme the United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT), will collaborate to obtain satellite images of the commissioned sites, museums and cities dating from both before and after the beginning of the hostilities (24 February 2022), thus providing pre-hostilities baseline images in order to conduct detailed analysis with the post-hostilities satellite images. This will allow UNESCO and UNITAR to determine the level, type of the damage, losses, or destructions, and also to analyse the sites’ and museums’ state of conservation, and ensure overall monitoring at the urban level.

The supported projects could include for example visual arts exhibitions, music concerts and performances, cultural and creative workshops, memorialization projects, film festivals, as well as research, archive and digitalization of creativity, across various cities of Ukraine and online. This support will help to promote the talents and voices of Ukrainian artists and cultural professionals, by enabling Ukrainian cultural and creative institutions to pursue their cultural activities and re-connect with their audiences and each other. Specific attention will also be put on gender mainstreaming in all projects, notably by privileging creative projects by women, projects that promote gender equality in the cultural and creative industries, and promoting the equal participation of women and men.

projects.name: Rebuilding the energy system in Ukraine under the carbon neutrality and just transition concepts
projects.description:
The objective of this project is to assess the size of the problem associated with rebuilding energy infrastructure in Ukraine and identify technology and policy options that need to be considered to design and implement a carbon neutral energy system. The project will assess the critical raw material (CRM) resource potential of Ukraine according to the United Nations Framework Classification of Resources (UNFC) and the United Nations Resource Management System (UNRMS) to support the low carbon energy transition. Attention is to be given to the social aspect of the proposed solutions. The project will assess various costs (social, economic, and environmental) that the suggested reconstruction strategy is likely to put on the local communities and social groups and explore measures that could be adopted to alleviate those negative impacts in the short, medium, and long term.
Proposed activities: 
A.1.1. Conduct analysis of the critical raw material resources in Ukraine following the United Nations Framework Classification for Resources (UNFC) and develop a report on the relevance of critical raw materials in the country to support its low carbon energy transition through the application of the United Nations Resource Management System (UNRMS). 
A.1.2. Online training workshop on the application of UNFC and UNRMS for critical raw material management in Ukraine. 
A1.3. Adapt the UNECE Framework on Carbon Neutrality to the conditions in Ukraine, develop a strategy (in a form of a report) for application of the adapted framework in the country, identifying the best technology and policy options to design a carbon neutral local energy system. 
A.1.4. Organize an online policy dialogue and launch UNECE partnership on rebuilding the Ukrainian energy system in accordance with the objectives of carbon neutrality and the concept of just transition.
A.2.1 Explore socio-economic aspects of the process of attaining a carbon neutral energy system in Ukraine, identify measures that need to be adopted in order to align the proposed strategy on attaining carbon neutrality with the premises of just transition (including gender equality), and develop a report summarizing the findings.

projects.name: Ensuring access to clean water in Ukraine: Water quality testing kits and portable laboratory kits for schools and local populations
projects.description:
Clean, safe water is essential for populations in conflict-affected areas and emergencies. In these areas, populations are exposed to higher risks of consumption of contaminated drinking water due to disruptions of water treatment and supply services, which may result in water-borne diseases. Consequently, access to safe drinking water is crucial for the survival of people living in conflict-affected areas, especially for children and women. It is vital for local populations to have the means to verify the quality and safety of the water they rely upon for drinking, cooking and personal hygiene when the access to water treatment and supply services is disrupted.
Consequently, UNESCO proposes the distribution of simple water quality testing kits and portable laboratory kits to schools and local communities in conflict-affected areas, as such kits provide vital information on the quality and safety of the water for the local populations and internally-displaced persons relying upon for drinking, cooking and personal hygiene during the conflict.

projects.name: UNESCO International Expert Mission to Assess Damage to Cultural and Religious Sites in Odesa
projects.description:
In line with its mandate under Article 23(.2) of the 1954 Hague Convention, UNESCO, on its own initiative, is establishing a UNESCO international expert group to conduct a technical assessment of damage inflicted on cultural and religious sites  in Odesa, as a result of the ongoing war, and in particular of the attacks perpetrated since 19 July 2023. 

The objectives of the mission are as follows:
(a)	Conduct a comprehensive technical assessment of the damage inflicted on cultural and religious properties in Odesa by the missile strikes carried out between 19 July 2023 and 23 July 2023. A comprehensive assessment shall include the following:
i.	Site inventory and documentation
ii.	Assessment of structural integrity assessment
iii.	Assessment of collections; 
(b)	Identify the immediate threats to the cultural and religious sites’ integrity and propose necessary measures to stabilize and protect them from further deterioration;
(c)	Identify lessons-learned to implement protection strategies to safeguard at-risk cultural property in Odesa in accordance with the provisions of the 1954 Hague Convention.
(d)	Preliminary assess the level of impact of the damage inflicted on the cultural and religious properties on the Outstanding Universal Value of the World Heritage property.

The project focuses on supporting the further development of professional skills of the internally displaced population to identify replacements for disrupted channels of incomes. Furthermore, the project contributes to the resilience of Ukrainian SMEs, primarily in the agribusiness sector, by building their capacities to sell online.

projects.name: Ukraine GovStack country package implementation
projects.description:
The GovStack initiative is a multi-stakeholder initiative led by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development, Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ), Estonia, the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), and the Digital Impact Alliance.  GovStack aims to accelerate the digital transformation of government services. The current engagement focuses on the Ukrainian Platform of Registers and has multiple milestones to be achieved. In the first phase, the difference between the technical requirements GovStack and the Platform of Registers is to be determined by the finalization of the Fit Gap Analysis launched in 2022. Based on the results of the Fit Gap Analysis, a GovStack-compliant prototype shall be developed and made available on the GovStack sandbox. Market research will complement this work by exploring the potential of the Platform of Registries implementation and use in other countries. 

These activities are implemented together and with the financial support of Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) on behalf of the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).
